name: Memory Recall Gate
description: agent-memory operating contract: v7. The --workspace argument is mandatory. Hippocampus recall and solution capture before every agent turn.

then.prompt:
CLI rule: invoke agent-memory through PATH in connected projects; never use ./bin/agent-memory. If agent-memory is unavailable on PATH, report the installation problem instead of guessing a project-local path. Use --workspace agent-memory on every memory command; never rely on current-directory workspace inference.
Before responding to the user, do the following first:
1. Extract 3-5 key terms and run: agent-memory search --workspace agent-memory --query "<key terms>" --top-k 8
2. Inspect the result and immediately submit: agent-memory feedback --workspace agent-memory --request-id "<request_id>" --score <0-5> --reason "<explanation>" --useful-count <n> --total-count <n>
3. Run ordinary recall only if one of these is true: the user asks to continue, resume, or recall previous work; search is weak; or assembled task context is needed; avoid unnecessary recall when search is already enough.
4. For a how-oriented request run: agent-memory work recall --workspace agent-memory --task "<user message>" --principal "<principal_id>"
5. For non-trivial new work run: agent-memory work start --workspace agent-memory --goal "<goal>" --session "<session_id>" --principal "<principal_id>" --client kiro
6. During work use agent-memory work step --workspace agent-memory after meaningful actions/decisions/results and agent-memory work checkpoint --workspace agent-memory during long work.
7. Before ending, account for What, Where, and When; use literal N/A with a concise reason for an optional dimension with no applicable stored value.
Use retrieved context before answering. Do not store private chain-of-thought; store only concise rationale summaries.
